parole.significato: bump (on an otherwise flat or even surface)
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch bulte, from Proto-West Germanic *bulti, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰel- (“to blow, inflate, swell”). Cognate with northern German Bult, Bülte.

parole.significato: horse-fly, blood-sucking fly of the family Tabanidae
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch dauese, probably from the adjectival sense (see Etymology 1). A direct descent from Proto-West Germanic *dawas, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰowos- (“botfly”), has also been proposed (Goossens 1985).

From Middle Dutch dêsem, from Old Dutch *thēsimo, from Proto-West Germanic *þaisimō, from Proto-Indo-European *teh₂-. Cognate with Old Saxon *thēsimo, Middle Low German dêsem, Old English þǣsma, Old High German deismo, Middle High German deisme, German Deisam.

Cognate with German jauchzen. The further etymology is not entirely clear. If the Dutch and German words are inherited from a common source, the word would be of Proto-West Germanic origin at the very latest, although it has been suggested that the Dutch word could represent a borrowing from German.

parole.significato: a jackdaw, the bird species Coloeus monedula, closely related to the crow, magpie and raven
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch cauwe, from Old Dutch *kāwa, from Proto-West Germanic *kahu (compare West Frisian ka), from Proto-Indo-European *gewH- (“to call, cry”) (compare Lithuanian giedóti, Tocharian A kāk (“he calls upon”), Sanskrit गायति (gāyati)).

From Middle Dutch crûke, from Old Dutch *crūca, from Proto-West Germanic *krūkā (“pot, pitcher”), of uncertain origin. Possibly from a Proto-Indo-European root shared with Old Armenian կարաս (karas, “pitcher, large jar”), Ancient Greek κρωσσός (krōssós, “pitcher”), but the phonetics are problematic.

parole.significato: wooden walkway over a creek, a duckboard
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch vlonder, from Old Dutch *flonder, from Proto-West Germanic *flonþr. Has also occasionally been seen as a by-form of vonder, but this is controversial. parole.significato: an orphan, person or animal having survived both parents
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch wêse, from Old Dutch wēso, from Proto-West Germanic *waisō, of uncertain origin, with no solid cognates outside of Germanic; possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁widʰéwh₂ (“widow”). parole.significato: sail of a windmill or blade on a wind turbine
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch wieke, from Proto-West Germanic *weukā (“flax bundle, wick”), from Proto-Indo-European *weg- (“to weave”).

parole.significato: shop, store (establishment that sells goods to the public)
parole.testo: From Middle Dutch winkel (“corner”), from Old Dutch winkel, from Proto-West Germanic *winkil, from Proto-Indo-European *weng- (“to bend, bow, arch, curve”). Cognate with German Winkel, Old English wincel. The meaning "shop" is derived from the meaning "corner in which merchandise is stalled".

From Middle Dutch sarp, from Old Dutch *sarp, from Proto-West Germanic *sarp. Cognate with Old High German sarf. From Middle Dutch sinken, from Old Dutch *sincan, from Proto-West Germanic *sinkwan, from Proto-Indo-European *sengʷ- (“to fall, sink”).
From Middle Dutch sinnen, from Old Dutch *sinnan, from Proto-West Germanic *sinnan, from Proto-Indo-European *sent-n-, a nasal suffix present from the root *sent- (“to feel”).
